It's possible to determine information regarding the multiplicities of the roots of a polynomial from its graph.

  • If the graph intersects the [MATH: x]-axis but is not tangent to the [MATH: x]-axis at [MATH: x=a,] we have a simple root [MATH: x=a.]

  • If the graph is tangent to the [MATH: x]-axis at [MATH: x=a,] we have a multiple root [MATH: x=a.] Furthermore:

    • If the graph touches the [MATH: x]-axis and reverses direction at [MATH: x=a,] the multiplicity of a root [MATH: x=a] is even.

    • If the graph crosses the [MATH: x]-axis at [MATH: x=a,] the multiplicity of a root [MATH: x=a] is odd.

In our case, the graph is tangent to the [MATH: x]-axis at [MATH: x=-4.] So, [MATH: x=-4] is a multiple root.

Furthermore, the graph touches the [MATH: x]-axis and reverses direction at [MATH: x=-4.] So, [MATH: x=-4] has even multiplicity.

Therefore, [MATH: x=-4] is a multiple root of even multiplicity.

sections.normalized_html:

Based on the graph, we can make the following conclusions about the multiplicities:

  • Since the graph is not tangent to the [MATH: x]-axis at [MATH: x =-2,] this root is a simple root (the multiplicity equals [MATH: 1]).

  • Since the graph just touches the [MATH: x]-axis and reverses direction at [MATH: x =-1,] this root has even multiplicity.

  • Since the graph passes through [MATH: x = 2,] this root has odd multiplicity, and since the graph is tangent to the [MATH: x]-axis at [MATH: x=2,] the multiplicity must be greater than one.

From the given options, the only possible equation is [MATH: y= (x+2)(x+1)^2(x-2)^3.]

Only graph [MATH: \textbf{III}] displays this end behavior. Therefore, the correct answer is [MATH: \textbf{III}].

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
It's possible to determine information regarding the multiplicities of the roots of a polynomial from its graph. We summarize all possible cases in the table below:

| [MATH: 1] / / (Simple root) | [IMG: /graphics/63f2b30ad86b6ceefb17b5b76e1e38f3] | [IMG: /graphics/6af2266b7f91657145ef859c5179437f] |

Content:
Note the following:

Content:
- The graph is tangent to the [MATH: x]-axis at multiple roots. This means that if [MATH: x=a] is a multiple root, then the graph of the polynomial is parallel to the [MATH: x]-axis at this point.
- If the multiplicity of a root [MATH: x=a] is even, the graph just touches the [MATH: x]-axis and reverses direction at [MATH: x=a.]
- If the multiplicity of a root [MATH: x=a] is odd (including a simple root of multiplicity [MATH: 1]), the graph crosses the [MATH: x]-axis at [MATH: x=a.]
- The graph of the polynomial is never tangent to the [MATH: x]-axis at simple roots.

Item 2 — Example: Identifying Multiplicity of a Root Given a Graph

Example Prompt:
[IMG: /graphics/ead16b30a111439d43b0f0b8024f158c]

A part of the graph of a polynomial [MATH: p(x)] is given above. Which of the following statements is true?

- [MATH: x=-4] is a multiple root of odd multiplicity
- [MATH: x=-4] is a multiple root of even multiplicity
- [MATH: x=-4] is a simple root

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
| Multiplicity | Sketch | Sketch |
| [MATH: 1] / / (Simple Root) | [IMG: /graphics/8d4fa6772f455694bd3de3902a20aeeb] | [IMG: /graphics/70231eae4f8dd6d1843bad449fc2e7c3] |
| [MATH: >1] / / (Multiple Root) / / Even | [IMG: /graphics/858c9a8ff00003e7465a1ff3ed7c096b] | [IMG: /graphics/53e2a4b825235fd256356c80c61c67cd] |
| [MATH: >1] / / (Multiple Root) / / Odd | [IMG: /graphics/3d1237ff3984c61c337993fffbfe9a3b] | [IMG: /graphics/b341a19379dc575c8b225b2b99d79689] |

It's possible to determine information regarding the multiplicities of the roots of a polynomial from its graph.

- If the graph intersects the [MATH: x]-axis but is not tangent to the [MATH: x]-axis at [MATH: x=a,] we have a simple root [MATH: x=a.]
- If the graph is tangent to the [MATH: x]-axis at [MATH: x=a,] we have a multiple root [MATH: x=a.] Furthermore:

- If the graph touches the [MATH: x]-axis and reverses direction at [MATH: x=a,] the multiplicity of a root [MATH: x=a] is even.
- If the graph crosses the [MATH: x]-axis at [MATH: x=a,] the multiplicity of a root [MATH: x=a] is odd.

In our case, the graph is tangent to the [MATH: x]-axis at [MATH: x=-4.] So, [MATH: x=-4] is a multiple root.

Furthermore, the graph touches the [MATH: x]-axis and reverses direction at [MATH: x=-4.] So, [MATH: x=-4] has even multiplicity.

Therefore, [MATH: x=-4] is a multiple root of even multiplicity.
